2) What is your budget range for inference costs (monthly) or target $/1M tokens you’re aiming for?
3) Any internal targets for CAC payback and gross margin per feature we should use for scenario modeling?

Next steps I propose:

Marissa — thanks for the recap, that aligns with our notes. Quick answers below so you can start modeling: 

1) Expected traffic (ballpark):
- Pilot (Q3): ~10–20k MAUs with heavy usage from a pilot cohort — roughly 50M tokens/month.
- Full rollout (Q4): 50k–200k MAUs translating to ~150M–200M tokens/month as we enable more features.

2) Target $/1M tokens: our procurement and finance teams are aiming for a $/1M range of approximately $1,200–$1,800 (we have some flexibility depending on committed volume and SLAs).

3) CAC payback and margin targets:
- Target CAC payback: 6–9 months for the new LLM-driven feature set.
- Target gross margin (post-inference and hosting costs) for these features: ~55–65%.

Additional context: revenue per feature (net) is modest initially — we expect $8–12 ARPU uplift per paid customer from the new features; so we need inference costs and CAC to fit within that envelope.

Happy to hop on a quick follow if that helps; otherwise send over your scenarios.

—Tom

Tom — perfect, this is exactly what we needed. I put together three short scenarios (pilot, steady-state conservative, steady-state aggressive) in the attached workbook so you can see how inference cost flows to $/feature and margin. A few notes and follow-ups I need from you to finalize: 

Attached: FintechX_unit_econ_model.xlsx (tabbed by scenario) and Redwood_pricing_sheet.pdf

Key assumptions I used in the workbook (please confirm/adjust):
- Token mix by feature: underwriting (40% tokens), recommendations (35%), summaries (25%).
- Model choice: medium-sized open model with Redwood’s standard hosted quantized runtime for pilot; we show dedicated capacity pricing for committed tiers.
- Baseline Redwood list: $/1M tokens = $2,000 (on-demand); committed tier examples show $1,500; deep commit shows $1,200.

What I need from you to refine:
1) Confirm avg tokens/session per feature (I used 120 tokens for underwriting, 45 for recs, 35 for summary).
2) Confirm expected conversion uplift and incremental ARPU per active user we should bake in (I used $9 net uplift in the model).
3) Confirm your CAC per new customer (or range) and payback window target (you noted 6–9 months — we’ll model both).

Preliminary outputs from the workbook (for discussion):
- Pilot (50M tokens/mo): estimated inference cost to FintechX using committed pilot pricing (pro-forma) ~$75k/month; that maps to ~$1,500 per $1M tokens in the pilot scenario after a small pilot discount.
- $/feature (per 1k users/month active): underwriting ~ $0.85 per active user, recommendations ~ $0.30, summaries ~ $0.24 (these convert from token consumption + model selection).
- CAC payback at current assumptions: with $9 uplift and $75k monthly inference cost, payback sits near 7–10 months depending on conversion.

If those outputs look reasonable, I’ll draft a pilot commercial: 3-month pilot at committed 50M tokens/month with a 12% pilot discount, then a 6–12 month committed tier with sliding discounts down to $1,200 per 1M at larger commits.

Thanks — attach here: FintechX_unit_econ_model.xlsx and Redwood_pricing_sheet.pdf

Best,
Marissa
